newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania 1997 exports expected to rise by 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania 1997 exports expected to rise by 2.5 pct.

text.p: Romania expects to increase the value of its exports by 2.5 percent this year after a 3.2 percent fall in 1996 and is aiming for an export growth rate of 5.0 percent by 2000, the government said on Monday.
"Exports will become a leverage to dynamise the economy and a source to fund spending on imports," said a document prepared by the government's Economic Reform Council.
It said exports would rise by 4.1 percent next year and by 5.0 percent in 1999 and also in 2000.
Imports, which saw a 3.0 percent slide in 1996, are forecast to slide by 1.9 percent this year, when Romania seeks to slash its bulging current account deficit.

The government document forecast a fall in Romania's trade balance -- with exports in FOB prices and imports in CIF prices -- to $1.95 billion this year from $2.3 billion in 1996. The trade gap is seen narrowing to $1.79 billion next year and to some $1.75 billion by 2000.
Latest data put Romania's trade balance deficit -- in FOB prices -- at $184.6 million in the first quarter of 1997, down from $403.3 million in the year-ago period.
